utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina, et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Gotovina Defence has asked an extension of time for submissions which were due today. Two days extension of time is granted. Mr. Vurnek, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Kuzmanovic, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There are just a couple of general topic areas that I wanted to discuss as a result of cross-examination by the Prosecutor and questions by the Bench. The first area concerns artillery which is where we left off, and your statement D1896 -- and your statement and D1896 which was the war path. You had discussed that there was a reconnaissance group and that reconnaissance group was used to correct artillery fire on the first day of the operation. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what your role was in that reconnaissance group on that first day and what kind of artillery we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the operative reconnaissance group was to detect and pin-point the exact positions of enemy forces, their fortified positions, to detect minefields and lay open a passage for their troops through the mind fields.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I spoke too quickly. I wanted to know your specific role and what you role you had, if any, with regard to that group.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I did not have a role to play in that group, since I was injured. When the commander of the group was killed, I took over the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the person -- you're familiar with what would need to be done to correct artillery fire; and the second part of that question that I asked initially was, what kind of artillery were we talking about on that first day, in terms of what would be corrected? What kind of artillery fire are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So we're not talking about any high-level Howitzers, or cannons from a distance; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with what the specific person would do with respect to artillery fire and correcting it, this mortar fire that you were talking about, what kind of tools would this person have to correct the fire? Would he have maps, would he have -- what would he do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to correct the mortar battery fire with any precision, it is necessary to have a topographical map and a compass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were those tools available to the person who was correcting the artillery fire, to your recollection, on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several persons from the group had both the maps of the area and compasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on to the issue of your interview and statement, which is D1895. Mr. Vurnek, did any investigator or lawyer at any time tell you what you had to say in that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The statement that you ended up signing, were those words yours, or were they someone else's words?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were my words in answer to questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you influenced in any way by any investigator or attorney to make your statement a certain way?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the topic of photographs. We spent a great deal of time on the issue of the black-and-white photographs that you saw before testifying, and I believe they were colour here in the courtroom. You were not in Gracac on the 9th of August when those photos were allegedly taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Markac Defence at any time ask you anything about those photos other than to ask you what your thoughts were as to what the photos depicted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to tell what the photographs stood for, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Markac Defence tell you what any other witness may have testified to regarding those photos?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move to the questions that the Prosecutor asked about two exhibits, which were statements given by Mr. Vanderostyne and Mr. Steenbergen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Those are P321 and P516. They don't necessarily need to be up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But in P321 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose I will have them up because I want to make sure that everything is read correctly and the Court can see that. If we can go to P321, please, page 6 of 14, paragraph 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown an article by Mr. Vanderostyne and your attention was drawn to portions of his statement, Mr. Vurnek. I'd like to show you paragraphs 18 and 19 of Mr. Vanderostyne's statement, and I'll read them, part of them anyway, to save time. Paragraph 18 says: "We then came in Otocac. I can see from my notes that my main focus was on the impact of the war. I saw all kinds of traces of demolition/firing, houses blown up, traces of artillery shelling, traces of war such as fresh destruction. In my notes, I stated that in every city in every village, and in every single hamlet I saw that Croatian soldiers had settled. You could tell that it was the end of the offensive. The soldiers were walking around in groups or sitting together. They were not in aggressive positions. I saw no Serb soldiers. My general perception was that the area was totally empty of Serbs." Now, before Operation Storm, Mr. Vurnek, are you familiar as to whether or not Otocac was entirely in Croatian hands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 19, it continued: "People told me that Otocac had been under fire on Saturday." Could you tell the Chamber whether or not that fire was fire from Serb positions? Saturday, being the second day of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the statement of Mr. Steenbergen, P516, paragraph 45. Mr. Vurnek, this is a statement on paragraph 45, excuse me, in which Mr. Vanderostyne [sic] states: "I first visited Gracac on 6th August." Now you were, Mr. Vurnek, in Gracac on the 6th of August; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: He further states in this paragraph: "We observed burned houses and houses that were still burning. It was difficult to distinguish between damage caused by shelling and damage caused by arson. We did not conduct any crater analysis at this time, but we could clearly see craters from shelling in various parts all over the town - most of the streets had some form of shelling damage. For example, there were roughly 10 to 20 craters observed in the area of the cross-roads I have marked with D on the map." Now, the first question I wanted to ask you is: With respect to your recollection on the 6th of August, other than the house that you saw when you entered Gracac, do you recall any burnt houses or houses that were still burning in Gracac itself, while you were in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any craters from shelling in various parts all over the town, as Mr. Vanderostyne stated -- or Mr. Steenbergen states in his statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw several craters at the cross-roads just outside of the town. As for the town itself, I don't recall there being any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to paragraph 51, please, which is the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 51 -- on the Croatian version, Mr. Vurnek, it will go from the first to the second page, or to the next page but I will just start at the beginning. On paragraph 51 the witness says in his statement: "I have been shown an UNMO HQ SS daily sitrep dated 6th August, 1995, and timed at 2030 hours which refers to HV troops looting empty houses in Gracac and the fact that the UNMO office in Gracac was burned to the ground. Later in this sitrep it is reported that UNMO team met with the commander of HV special forces and were allowed to patrol in Gracac. Whilst patrolling in Gracac, UNMO Team Gracac observed HV troops looting and that all houses in Gracac are partially destroyed and five of the houses are completely destroyed." I wanted to ask you, Mr. Vurnek, based on your observations on the 6th of August, 1995, when you were in Gracac itself, did you observe any troops of any kind - whether they were special police troops, HV troops - looting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't observe anyone looting any property in Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, later in the last sentence this witness says: "... all the houses in Gracac are partially destroyed ..." Did you observe any of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day of my testimony, I said that I saw one house on the edge of Gracac having been destroyed, burnt. I didn't see any other destruction, save for the fact that the whole town was in a state of neglect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, there is no definition of what "partially destroyed" is, but in your observation, in Gracac, did any house that you saw appear to you to be in any state of destruction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. Except for that one house, I don't recall others being destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go, please, to D443.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- you started saying that there's no definition of "partial destruction," and the witness said at the end that he doesn't have any recollection of destroyed houses which may create some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see any houses which were -- which had, well, let's say, serious or substantial damage without being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except for the house I mentioned, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Please pull up D433. Sorry. 443. If I said 433, I'm sorry. That's not it. It was right the first time. I mis-numbered it in my notes. It's D433. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, this is a map which has been marked and admitted as evidence of Gracac and the surrounding areas with a legend marking various points on the map. Now, with the assistance of the usher, I would like you to show us where your unit entered the road going from the upper left of the map down to Gracac. Before do you that, is that the road from Gracac to Gospic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark in blue where your unit came upon that road and then from that point you went into Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have the usher's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a very imprecise map. I can only give you an approximation --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the route of advancement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All I want for you -- from you, Mr. Vurnek, is an approximation of where we -- there we go. So essentially you were right very close by to Sveti Rok.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And from that point where the tip of your arrow is your unit advanced on that road all the way to Gracac on the 5th of August; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, did you -- how did you get into Gracac? Was that by -- on foot?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, myself, yes, went there on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you along the road as you went to Gracac. Along that road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to please show the witness a short video of that route taken on the 5th of August. Oh, can we please tender this document with the map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Say 5th of August, may I take it 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Before we do that, before we show the video, Your Honour, may I please tender the map with the marking by the witness. MS. DE LANDRI: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D1899. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1899 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There is some brief dialogue on this. The booth has been provided with copies, Your Honour, it's 65 ter 3D00140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which route do we -- will be shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: From Sveti Rok to Gracac. We could do it through Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, I just want you to watch this video, and then I will ask you some questions about it. It's very short. After it's done playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Please play the video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The tank looks as if it has been used as fire for a barbecue. "Sveti Rok. "Sempre Gracac. Here we go. This could be Ricice, which was also a Croatian village. "As soon as you see everything is burnt, you know that it is our village. Clear. It's been burnt long ago. "This is all really been torched. "So where is now that fucking UNPROFOR to ask those ... [inaudible] ... "On a bicycle, right? "This is the UNPROFOR base. "Is this where we're going to go home through? "Pub. "Joco cafe. "Perhaps we should call home."

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you saw, obviously it wasn't the whole route from Sveti Rok to Gracac, but was that the route that you had mostly walked on the way to Gracac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the road we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that video -- do you recall seeing those homes on either side of the road that were shown, many of which, or most of which look like they had been significantly or completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what did those houses appear to you to be in terms of state of disrepair? Recently destroyed, currently destroyed? Based on your recollection of walking along that road.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't thinking it. We knew that those houses belonged to the Croats who had lived there before the war which had been destroyed in the early 1990s by the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So essentially the route that you took from Sveti Rok all the way through to Gracac, the destruction that you saw was destruction from long ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither our army nor police engaged in any fighting in that area. There was no fighting in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I understand that. But my -- my question to you, Mr. Vurnek, was essentially the route that you took from Sveti Rok all the way to Gracac, the destruction that you saw was destruction from long ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. There was vegetation and trees growing out of the houses. You could tell that they had been destroyed several years back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this video. MS. DE LANDRI: Could I ask the witness a few questions about the video, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take that in further cross -- or would you before you make up your mind as far as objections are concerned? MS. DE LANDRI: Well, I'm sure any foundation has been laid for the admission of it. And I can do it at the Court's preference. I can ask the questions in further examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we mark it identification and then see whether there is any objection at the very end. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we could also check, I have a recollection of this video having been ... I see, I guess it was marked but not admitted, so I take it back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll have to -- but if it was marked, any recollection as what number was there? So that we also can verify why it was not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was D294, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D294. We will look further into the matter. You can put further questions to the witness in recross. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all the questions I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Those are all the questions. Well, then, that moment has come very quickly. Mr. Vurnek, you will further be examined by Ms. De Landri. Please proceed. MS. DE LANDRI: Just a few questions about this video. Further cross-examination by Ms. De Landri:

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen it before today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information about how it was made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was involved in making the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So today is the first time that you've seen it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you can't identify any -- any persons who were involved in this video, in making the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone making it or recording it. You can re-wind, perhaps I can watch it again if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No. What I'm trying to ascertain is aside from your recollection of the events of August 5th, does the video add anything to your recollection of those events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is a fact, however, that this does refresh my memory somewhat, because a lot of time has elapsed between now and then. MS. DE LANDRI: Your Honour, I don't have any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just for the benefit of the parties, this was discussed at page 4827, beginning at line 20, on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you happen to a have a date and witness for me, Mr. Misetic, that would help? Because only for the later I have the page numbering and the...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have -- the date is the 11th June, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may further assist, there was also a discussion and it was tendered on the 2nd of June at transcript reference 4067, and the issue was that when it was put to the witness who testified then, Mr. Vanderostyne, Mr. Vanderostyne could not recognise any of these. So I think for the sake of completeness, the reference that Mr. Misetic gave, in combination with the one I just gave, will give the Chamber the full picture of that video and what the issues were when it was tendered and then not admitted by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just re-read what was said on page 4827. So at the time Mr. Vanderostyne, he couldn't say anything about the video. He was not familiar in any way. This witness -- but, Ms. De Landri, first of all, does -- is there any objection? Let's have that clear to start with. MS. DE LANDRI: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what the objection exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There is no foundation for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what is no foundation? What do you mean by "foundation"? That we do not know who made it? MS. DE LANDRI: Well, that's one of the objections. And the witness can testify from his personal recollection of those events. He has a personal recollection of the events of August 5th and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If someone would show me the video of my native town, even without knowing who made it, isn't it true that I could recognise certain features, and that in saying nothing was -- this is how it looked like, and then if see it, I could say, yes, that's -- that's not only a description of what it looked like but that is the picture of what it looked like. I recognise that. Would that be insufficient for admission? MS. DE LANDRI: Yes. The evidence would be your recollection and your testimony about the recollection. But not the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if ... if my testimony is that what I see now is what I described before and what I recognise as what -- what was in my native town, would you then withhold from the trier of fact that picture? MS. DE LANDRI: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And on what basis? MS. DE LANDRI: If there were insufficient information, indeed, no information about how the video was obtained, how it was made, the circumstances under which it was made, and the witness and this witness and another witness who came before the Chamber could not authenticate it, then I'd say it is not admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under what Rule in this Tribunal? MS. DE LANDRI: Rule 89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any case law in respect -- MS. DE LANDRI: I would have to check into that, Your Honour, but I would be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further response in relation to this objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing I would say is that the witness stated that this was the route that he took. He walked the route. The photographs helped his recollection as to what he talked about. There was evidence put to the witness in his cross-examination that the Croats had destroyed everything on each side of the road from Gospic to Gracac, and his testimony and the video serve to counteract that testimony. So I believe that the witness by looking at the video, and describing what he -- and commenting on the video confirms essentially what his testimony was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We would agree, Mr. President, there is -- the witness has laid foundation. I think under the rules of the Tribunal it is admissible, and even under common law if a witness testifies in Court that something fairly and accurately depicts what his recollection was, it would be admissible even in common law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I learned that the common law doesn't exist. That is one thing that is for sure. So in your common law, it would be admissible; in your common law, it would not be admissible, Ms. De Landri. Yes, yes. Your common law, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It would certainly be admissible, and I have got nothing further to add to the very eloquent arguments already expressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The Chamber will consider the matter. We will compare our common laws and our civil laws in the case law of the Tribunal. Mr. Vurnek, in respect of this matter, have you travelled that route often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: More than at that one occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say. Several times, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you recognise the overall picture, the general impression, or did you recognise specific houses or specific places when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Generally speaking, I recognised the route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I add just one question to what you had said regarding what was seen in the video by Mr. Vurnek? It might enhance the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I was focussing not on -- of course, we can see that sometimes you see this is the direction to Gracac. That is -- we have seen that as well. But what I wanted to know is when looking at houses on portions of the video where there's not included a traffic sign, whether he there recognised the overall picture or whether he recognised specific houses, specific villages. That was my question. And that's the way you understood it, I take it, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That must be the same road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked whether that's how you understood my question, but ... Any further questions in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, there was a comment in the video about what appeared to be the UN base. Do you recall that UN base being on the side of the road, as it was depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My recollection on whether we have already in evidence where that exactly was, I think it was marked on one of these maps with A2, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can -- I know the name of the place. We can ask the witness if he knew where it was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if he knows the name -- Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could tell us the name of that place, that would certainly assist us in later evaluating the evidence. Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UN base was in Gracac, on the outskirts of Gracac to one's left side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One other question. You said you saw one house burning close to where there was a weapon depot. Has the finding this weapons depot, has that been reported? Is there any document in which you say, Look there, there are the weapons to be found, or ... any reporting on paper for that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain. I think it exists. In any case, I reported that to my commander via my hand-held radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection exactly where that house was that you saw being on fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I remember it was in the immediate vicinity of the base we saw on the footage, perhaps a few hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But would you be able to identify it on a map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we then have the map? I have forgotten the number. But we saw recently the map, the one marked with the cross-roads marked on it. Mr. Kuzmanovic, could you assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll look for it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not the one that we saw today; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I think it's the one we saw yesterday, where the various places in Gracac were marked. Or the map underlying that marked map without any markings would be good as well. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think P536.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P536. Let's have a look that and see whether that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that is the one Mr. Waespi used in cross-examination of another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have P536 on the screen. Mr. Vurnek, on this map, could you identify where, approximately, you saw the house burning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I cannot be completely certain, but I think it was somewhere around this part. I believe so. In any case, I cannot be certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that you started marking. Is that -- is it true that you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drew a circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is only conditional, as I said. Cannot be completely precise on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You drew a circle. Could you make it a clear cross and preferably in red, I think, was the -- Madam Usher, could you assist the witness in -- with marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the official Defence colour is blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, blue, then nevertheless, I'd like to -- Could you put a thick cross, the place you marked, because there were earlier markings on this map. And could you add a letter X next to that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, to repeat, this is approximately the location that I saw it, as far as I can remember. It was on the south side of the road, where the house was that was in flames.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that marking. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we make this a Defence exhibit because it just clarifies part of the -- of the answers given in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number, Mr. Registrar, would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1900. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1900 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It appears that there are no further questions for the witness. Mr. Vurnek, this concludes your testimony. I would like thank you very much for coming to The Hague. It's a long way from where you live, for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions by the parties, questions by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the application for protective measures. The Chamber has decided that we will hear the witness of Witness MM-025 in closed session. Reasons to follow. In view of the time, if at all possible, the Chamber would want to see whether we can conclude with this witness today. And I especially draw the attention of the parties to the fact that what is already in the written statement, of course, now and then you need to give a bit of context, but, then, of course, the Chamber is fully aware of that, and that needs not to be repeated only if there is a clear need for context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm hoping that I will get done in a session. In light of the difficulties that the witness had, I'm going to do my best to do that so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we turn into closed session. It's a pity for the audience. They just arrived, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, of course, the curtains should be open. If I could seek the assistance, the joint assistance, this is a joint enterprise. We'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, 16th of December, 9.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of December, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
